data.message: Retrieving the official financial statement PDF from the CSE document repository
Document secured and staged for processing
Running multi-dimensional financial health diagnostics with LLM (this may take a minute)...
Health diagnostics finalised for JKH.N0000 — overall score: 66/100 · Fair

standardHealthChecks.name: Liquidity Health
standardHealthChecks.description: The Group maintains a Current Ratio of 1.07 (Current Assets of Rs. 237.0B vs. Current Liabilities of Rs. 221.8B) and a Quick Ratio of 0.83. Short-term liquidity is constrained by substantial bank overdrafts (Rs. 54.1B) and short-term borrowings (Rs. 55.7B).

standardHealthChecks.name: Profitability Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Group revenue increased by 24% YoY to Rs. 141.65B and EBITDA grew by 26% to Rs. 16.35B. However, net profit attributable to equity holders was heavily compressed at Rs. 62.2M due to Rs. 1.89B in net forex losses (mainly from City of Dreams USD debt) and elevated finance costs.

standardHealthChecks.name: Debt Management
standardHealthChecks.description: Total interest-bearing debt stands at Rs. 243.3B across long-term and short-term facilities. EBITDA-to-finance-cost coverage sits at ~2.01x (EBITDA Rs. 16.35B vs. Finance Costs Rs. 8.12B), but operating profit coverage is under 1.0x, exposing the Group to rate and currency risks.

standardHealthChecks.name: Cash Flow Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Net operating cash flow recorded strong growth, rising 226% YoY to Rs. 12.33B (up from Rs. 3.78B in Q1 2025/26), supported by Rs. 17.35B in cash generated from operations before working capital adjustments.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Segment EBITDA Growth & Diversification
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Group EBITDA grew 26% YoY, led by significant gains in Transportation (+223% to Rs. 5.01B) via Lanka Marine Services and CWIT port terminal ramp-up, as well as Property (+358%), offsetting Middle East conflict pressures on Leisure.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: As a diversified conglomerate, broad segment contribution buffers group performance against sector-specific macroeconomic headwinds.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Retail & Supermarket Operational Efficiency
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Keells Supermarkets generated same-store sales growth of 13%, driven by average basket value growth of 7% and customer footfall growth of 6%. Segment EBITDA expanded 16% to Rs. 2.83B.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Retail represents over 54% of Group Revenue, making store productivity and basket size growth key indicators of core consumer health.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Foreign Exchange & Currency Exposure Risk
dynamicHealthChecks.description: The Group carries a net foreign currency exposure of approximately USD 100M. Rupee depreciation (Rs. 337/USD vs Rs. 315/USD) caused a net forex loss of Rs. 3.83B on the City of Dreams USD term loan facility alone.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Heavy reliance on foreign-denominated project debt leaves bottom-line net profit highly sensitive to local currency depreciation.

recommendations: Implement currency hedging or balance-sheet structuring strategies for USD-denominated long-term liabilities at Waterfront Properties (City of Dreams Sri Lanka) to reduce bottom-line earnings volatility.
Refinance or consolidate short-term debt and bank overdraft facilities (Rs. 109.8B combined) into longer-tenor, fixed-rate debt to lower annual finance costs (Rs. 8.12B in Q1).
Accelerate operational ramp-up, occupancy, and average room rate (ARR) expansion across the integrated resort components at City of Dreams Sri Lanka to cover high depreciation and interest drag.
Maintain cost containment and energy-efficiency measures in Maldivian Resorts to counter heightened fuel costs and geopolitical travel sentiment disruptions.
result.analysisNotes: John Keells Holdings PLC exhibits strong operational revenue (+24%) and underlying cash EBITDA (+26%) expansion. However, reported profit after tax remains tightly squeezed by foreign exchange translation losses on foreign currency loans and heavy finance expenses. Operating cash generation remains healthy.
